pull.title: BIP458: Schnorr (Incremental) Half Aggregation
pull.body:
This implements BIP458: https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2205

The original version of this code ported over the work from b-wagn in https://github.com/BlockstreamResearch/secp256k1-zkp/pull/261

events.body: Rebased on the musig changes and added the compile options for cmake

Rebased to take into account the latest changes to cmake, CI and test framework. Also squashed the commit since maintaining them was annoying and there wasn't really a good reason for them. It was more of a crutch for me while I was taking my first steps here.
Rebased and added the test vectors from the BIP draft: https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2205
Addressed the feedback from @theStack and rebased, happy to remove the experimental status if reviewers think it doesn't apply here.
Changed the tag to include the BIP number

The vector generator breaks on the BIP's new size vectors, and `inc_aggregate` differs from the BIP when `n_before` is 0.

I ran the vectors of bitcoin/bips#2205 at 2f436b0 through the module, and 300 random cases against an implementation I maintain, on btclib-ecc. 36 of the 37 vectors the C API can express pass, and the random cases agree byte for byte, including corrupted inputs and s ≥ n. Results are the same on a local merge with master.

Rerunning `tools/test_vectors_halfagg_generate.py` on that BIP head writes the eight new size vectors into fixed-size arrays. The too-long ones fail the build under `-Werror`. The too-short ones are zero-padded without a warning, so aggregate vector 9, a 31-byte key, succeeds and the test aborts. The generator could skip them, as it skips incaggregate 4 to 6. The vector left, incaggregate 6, is skipped because `inc_aggregate` ignores the input `s` when `n_before` is 0, while the BIP adds it and fails when it is ≥ n. With `s = 1`, the C result verifies and the BIP's does not. `aggregate` relies on this, passing its output buffer as the input. Zeroing those 32 bytes in `aggregate`, as the BIP's `Aggregate` does, would let `inc_aggregate` read `s`. Otherwise the header could say `s` is ignored there. I measured through ctypes and can share the script.

events.body:
Rebased

> The vector generator breaks on the BIP's new size vectors

The latest update of the BIP just wasn't pulled in yet. I updated the vectors to the latest version of the BIP. The generator now skips the size vectors.

> `inc_aggregate` differs from the BIP when `n_before` is 0

I addressed this. `inc_aggregate` now always reads `s`, and `aggregate` starts from `s = 0` through a shared internal helper instead of zeroing the buffer. Vector 6 is also no longer skipped.

Concept ACK

One issue should be fixed before merge: `doc/halfagg.md` says that aggregating an invalid signature gives an invalid aggregate. That holds for one invalid input, but two can cancel out, as BIP 458 warns under both Aggregate and IncAggregate.

At ac35c4a83d7effb33180a30679dfa3fb1aefffcf, two signatures that each fail `secp256k1_schnorrsig_verify` aggregate into a signature that `secp256k1_schnorrsig_aggverify` accepts, in 100 of 100 random cases. I add d to one s and subtract d/z1 from the other, leaving the weighted sum unchanged. Readers may take a valid aggregate as proof that every input was valid, since the doc asks for individual checks only to find which signature failed. The sentence could follow the BIP: a valid aggregate does not prove valid inputs, so inputs that must be valid are verified individually first.

Both points of my earlier comment are fixed. `inc_aggregate` now reads the input s when `n_before` is 0, and the generator rebuilds `vectors.h` byte for byte from bitcoin/bips#2205's vectors at fe78361, incaggregate vector 6 included. Through ctypes, I compared the module with btclib-ecc, an independent implementation: in 300 random cases the two give the same bytes for aggregation and for incremental aggregation from an input s and reject the same input s ≥ n, and in the 267 non-empty ones they accept or reject the same valid and corrupted aggregates. At the previous head the same script fails all 300 cases with an input s. `tests`, the example and the benchmark pass on macOS arm64. Scripts and output: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/aba13d49caf4e9d0bdbdb3354b7fb100/2aadc3e1529cb27af32c0432323a9d8f09cdbb5a

events.body:
> `doc/halfagg.md` says that aggregating an invalid signature gives an invalid aggregate. That holds for one invalid input, but two can cancel out

Updated the doc to say that a valid aggregate does not imply valid input signatures.

ACK c371cec84c6cfacfe6aace890644b9b6724ae932

I read `main_impl.h`, `tests_impl.h`, the header, the example and the benchmark against BIP 458 and its `halfagg.py` at fe78361, and found no defect in the code. The hash order, the fixed first randomizer, the range checks and the verification equation match the BIP. Lengths and counts are checked before any read or write. I did not read the generator or the data in `vectors.h`, which regenerates byte for byte.

Only the doc sentence changed since my last review, and it is now correct: invalid inputs crafted to cancel verify in 100 of 100 cases through `aggregate` and through `inc_aggregate`, and without the cancelling input they are rejected in 200 of 200. The 300 random cases against btclib-ecc, an independent implementation, still agree. All 256 ctest tests pass on macOS arm64. Under ASan and UBSan, all but the exhaustive test pass, and so do 754 checks of a harness using exact-size heap buffers, including failed calls leaving the output untouched. Of 26 mutations of `main_impl.h`, the module's tests catch 24. One survivor accepts r ≥ p; I see no feasible signature that would tell it apart. Scripts and output: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/75c48df66cf2b0fa2d666bf0bbf80a02/fb73252aaa096f790fb6a60446aaced7da8cec1c

Not blocking: the other survivor removes `aggverify`'s s range check. `test_schnorrsig_aggregate_overflow` sets s to all 0xFF, which fails either way, and no vector catches it. `aggverify(CTX, NULL, NULL, 0, order, 32) == 0` with s equal to the group order does: I ran it, and it passes now and fails without the check. In `test_schnorrsig_aggregate_unforge`, the first case passes `sizeof(aggsig)` as the length, so 1002 of 1024 runs were rejected on length alone; `32*(n+1)` would fix that.

+#ifndef SECP256K1_SCHNORRSIG_HALFAGG_H
+#define SECP256K1_SCHNORRSIG_HALFAGG_H
+
+#include "secp256k1.h"
+#include "secp256k1_extrakeys.h"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif

+/** This module implements incremental (Half-)Aggregation of Schnorr
+ *  signatures as specificed by the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal draft
+ *  "Half-Aggregation of BIP 340 signatures"
+ *  (https://github.com/BlockstreamResearch/cross-input-aggregation/blob/master/half-aggregation.mediawiki).
+ */
+
+/** (Half-)Aggregate a sequence of Schnorr signatures.
+ *
+ *  Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
+ *  Args:           ctx: a secp256k1 context object.
+ *  Out:         aggsig: pointer to an array of aggsig_len many bytes to
+ *                       store the serialized aggregate signature. The size
+ *                       is expected to be 32*(n+1) bytes.
+ *  In/Out:  aggsig_len: size of the aggsig array that is passed in bytes;
+ *                       will be overwritten to be the exact size of aggsig.
+ *  In:         pubkeys: Array of n many x-only public keys.
+ *                       Can only be NULL if n is 0.
+ *               msgs32: Array of n many 32-byte messages.
+ *                       Can only be NULL if n is 0.
+ *               sigs64: Array of n many 64-byte signatures.
+ *                       Can only be NULL if n is 0.
+ *                    n: number of signatures to be aggregated.
+ */
+SECP256K1_API int secp256k1_schnorrsig_aggregate(
+    const secp256k1_context *ctx,
+    unsigned char *aggsig,
+    size_t *aggsig_len,
+    const secp256k1_xonly_pubkey *pubkeys,
+    const unsigned char *msgs32,
+    const unsigned char *sigs64,
+    size_t n
+) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(1) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(2) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(3);
+
+/** Incrementally (Half-)Aggregate a sequence of Schnorr
+ *  signatures to an existing half-aggregate signature.
+ *
+ *  Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
+ *  Args:           ctx: a secp256k1 context object.
+ *  In/Out:      aggsig: pointer to the serialized aggregate signature
+ *                       that is input. The first 32*(n_before+1) of this
+ *                       array should hold the input aggsig. It will be
+ *                       overwritten by the new serialized aggregate signature.
+ *                       It should be large enough for that, see aggsig_len.
+ *           aggsig_len: size of aggsig array in bytes.
+ *                       Should be large enough to hold the new
+ *                       serialized aggregate signature, i.e.,
+ *                       should satisfy aggsig_len >= 32*(n_before+n_new+1).
+ *                       It will be overwritten to be the exact size of the
+ *                       resulting aggsig.
+ *  In:     all_pubkeys: Array of (n_before + n_new) many x-only public keys,
+ *                       including both the ones for the already aggregated signature
+ *                       and the ones for the signatures that should be added.
+ *                       Can only be NULL if n_before + n_new is 0.
+ *           all_msgs32: Array of (n_before + n_new) many 32-byte messages,
+ *                       including both the ones for the already aggregated signature
+ *                       and the ones for the signatures that should be added.
+ *                       Can only be NULL if n_before + n_new is 0.
+ *           new_sigs64: Array of n_new many 64-byte signatures, containing the new
+ *                       signatures that should be added. Can only be NULL if n_new is 0.
+ *             n_before: Number of signatures that have already been aggregated
+ *                       in the input aggregate signature.
+ *                n_new: Number of signatures that should now be added
+ *                       to the aggregate signature.
+ */
+SECP256K1_API int secp256k1_schnorrsig_inc_aggregate(
+    const secp256k1_context *ctx,
+    unsigned char *aggsig,
+    size_t *aggsig_len,
+    const secp256k1_xonly_pubkey* all_pubkeys,
+    const unsigned char *all_msgs32,
+    const unsigned char *new_sigs64,
+    size_t n_before,
+    size_t n_new
+) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(1) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(2) SECP256K1_ARG_NONNULL(3);
+
+/** Verify a (Half-)aggregate Schnorr signature.
+ *

could use the `secp256k1_gej_eq_var` helper here which does the some steps internally:
```suggestion
    return secp256k1_gej_eq_var(&lhs, &rhs);
```

could use `secp256k1_sha256_initialize_midstate` here (introduced in PR https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1825, commit https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/commit/f48b1bfa5d40a4d7303b196017d2e298520d1066), see other modules that use BIP340 tagged hashes
this function was removed in #1908, so there is a (silent) merge conflict

comments.body:
Yeah, I myself argued that it might be possible to remove the category at some IRC meeting or the in-person meeting probably about a year ago. This was about the batch module specifically that still had it and it made sense for me to remove it there because it was already in BIP340 and the code would only be merged if it was in a usable state anyway, the bar is just that high already. I think @sipa said the category should be kept around if we want to introduce a module where the API may still change, at least that's the only argument I remember from the conversation. I already considered removing the category here and in fullagg for the same reasons as batch but then reconsidered: Maybe we would want to set it for some code that is specifically added for a soft fork before the soft fork is actually activated? (There are other use cases outside of consensus for halfagg and fullagg but realistically those will not get these PRs merged here.) I also saw that the Schnorr module was also merged as experimental but I did not go the extra mile to ask if this was actually because of the consensus angle, but I did the lazy thing and made no change here :)

However, I just now did some more digging and found this comment from @sipa that clarifies the intention for BIP340 at the time: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/817#issuecomment-693033273 The whole issue was actually just closed after we discussed it as a group, btw.

I am currently basically 50/50 because I think the arguments for keeping Schnorr experimental from the comment very much apply to this pull here as is. But on the other hand I think the pull has a very low chance of getting merged while these arguments still apply because of the high standard here and if we agree on that we can remove the status already. Well, there is a chance that an alternative, newly discovered use case becomes strong enough for an earlier merge so maybe 51/49 for keeping it experimental for now and potentially removing it before the merge if doesn't seem needed anymore.

That's a long way of saying, I am happy to remove or keep it around.
